newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore gas oil swaps down as India cancels tender.
newsitem.headline: S'pore gas oil swaps down as India cancels tender.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Sept 17 (Reuter) Singapore gas oil swaps fell sharply on news that India had cancelled its tender to buy high speed diesel for November delilvery, traders said on Tuesday.
"The market was traded down aggressively as a result of this news as India had not cancelled a monthly buy tender so far this year," one trader said.
October gas oil swaps traded earlier this afternoon at $26.75 and $26.72, down from the mid-day quotes of $27.15-27.25, one broker said.
Brokers last quoted October swaps at $26.70-26.78.

Gas oil swaps opened this morning to trade to a low of $26.80 on the back of big drops to overnigh crude values. But prices bounced back up as more buyers emerged. At noon brokers valued the market at $27.20.
"There are three big buyers in Asia and if one of them is not buying it is definitely very bearish news to the market," one trader said.
Apart from India, China and Indonesia are the region's two other big gas oil buyers.
Players had initially counted on the market getting strong support at around $27.00 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore but with this news they are no longer as confident.
